originality.rationale: The classical a=2 complete-moduli theorem is pre-existing and explicitly excluded from novelty. The present claim is a complete variable-even-base classification with arbitrary products of primes dividing a+1 and an isolated 3 branch, plus two valuation-isometric residue permutations. Closest original paper and differently parameterized k-Jacobsthal paper inspected; targeted searches found no dominating theorem, with acknowledged unindexed general Lucas risk.
residual_risks: A general classification of complete residue moduli for Lucas U(P,Q) sequences could subsume the split-root specialization despite differing keywords.
Closest classical paper gives only issue-month May 2015; the fully dated initial source is a distinct but related March 18, 2015 arXiv recurrence study.
A differently named generalized-Jacobsthal or integer-valued-polynomial permutation theorem may cover some results.

value.rationale: Complete residue systems for Jacobsthal numbers are an explicit published mathematical problem, and the parameterized family exhibits new structural regimes: multi-prime moduli 3^u5^v at a=14, an isolated prime-3 exception at a=6, and parity-wise isometric equidistribution on every supported odd modulus. This is a uniform complete arithmetic classification, not a finite census or an automatic numeric substitution. The classical a=2 slice has no independent novelty claim.
